questions.question: The amount of force needed to accelerate a 10 kg mass at 2.5m/s² is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

To find the amount of force needed to accelerate a mass, we use** Newton's second law of motion**, which states: F= ma

Where:

__
 
• F is the force,
 
• m is the mass,
 
• a is the acceleration.

Given:

 
• m = 10 kg,
 
• a= 2.5 m/s²,

We can calculate F as follows:

 F=10 Kg times 2.5 m/s²= 25N

Therefore, the force needed is **25 N**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Force is an interaction that, when unopposed, will change the motion of an object.
 
• A force can cause an object with mass to change its velocity (which includes to begin moving from a state of rest), i.e., to accelerate.
 
• Force is a **vector **quantity, meaning it has** both magnitude and direction**.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**
 
 
• It states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object times its acceleration ( F= ma).
 
• This law explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force.
 
 
 
• **Mass:**
 
 
• Mass is a property of a physical body and a measure of its resistance to acceleration when a force is applied.
 
• The mass of an object also determines the strength of its gravitational attraction to other bodies.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change in the velocity of an object with respect to time.

questions.question: Average velocity of a body can be given by the arithmetic mean of initial velocity and final velocity for a given period of time when the body is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**moving with uniform acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average velocity** is calculated as the arithmetic mean of the **initial velocity** and **final velocity** when the body is moving under **uniform acceleration**.
 
• This is because under **uniform acceleration**, the change in velocity is linear and equally distributed over time.
 
• The formula for average velocity in this case is: **(Initial velocity + Final velocity) / 2**.
 
• Uniform acceleration implies that the rate of change of velocity is constant during the given period of time.
 
• This relationship holds true for motion in a straight line, such as a body falling under the influence of **gravity** (ignoring air resistance).
 
• For example, in cases like the motion of a car accelerating uniformly or free-fall motion, this method of calculating average velocity can be applied.
 
• If the acceleration is not uniform, this formula does not apply, and the average velocity must be calculated by integrating the velocity function over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Moving with non-uniform acceleration**__

 __
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration** refers to a situation where the rate of change of velocity is not constant.
 
• In this case, the velocity changes irregularly over time, and the average velocity cannot be determined using the simple arithmetic mean formula.
 
• Instead, the average velocity must be calculated by integrating the velocity function over the time interval.
 
 
 
• **Moving with uniform speed**__
 __
 
• **Uniform speed** implies that the body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• In this case, the average velocity is the same as the constant speed, and there is no variation in velocity to consider.
 
 
 
• **Moving with uniform velocity**__
 
 
• **Uniform velocity** means that both the speed and direction of motion remain constant throughout the period of time.
 
• Since there is no change in velocity, the initial velocity equals the final velocity, and the average velocity will be the same as the constant velocity.

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upwards and rises to a height of 20 m. The approximate initial velocity of the ball is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Equations of Motion under Gravity:**

__
 
• The motion of objects under the influence of gravity can be described using the equations of motion.
 
• For an object thrown vertically upward, the final velocity at the highest point is zero.
 
• Formula: v² = u² + 2as
 
• Here, **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, **a** is acceleration (due to gravity), and **s** is the displacement.
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g):** The acceleration imparted to objects due to the gravitational force. SI unit: m/s². Dimensional Formula: [LT⁻²]. g ≈ 9.8 m/s².

**Calculation:**__

Given,

Mass of the ball, m = 0.5 kg (Not required for calculation)

Maximum height, s = 20 m

Final velocity at the highest point, v = 0 m/s

Acceleration due to gravity, a = -9.8 m/s² (negative as it is upward motion)

Using the equation of motion:

v² = u² + 2as

Substitute the given values:

0 = u² + 2(-9.8)(20)

⇒ 0 = u² - 392

⇒ u² = 392

⇒ u = sqrt{392}

⇒ u ≈ 19.8 {m/s}

**∴ The initial velocity of the ball is approximately 20 m/s.**

• **Free Fall**

• In a vacuum, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass.

• Terminal velocity is the constant speed that a freely falling object eventually reaches when the resistance of the medium prevents further acceleration.
 
• At terminal velocity, the force of gravity is balanced by the drag force of the medium.

questions.question: A car moving along a straight path slows down and stops. The car is under which type of motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-uniform motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A car slowing down and eventually stopping is an example of **non-uniform motion**, where the speed of the car changes over time.
 
• In non-uniform motion, the velocity of the object is not constant, and there is an acceleration or deceleration involved.
 
• This type of motion can be described by the change in speed and direction, indicating a varying rate of displacement.
 
• Non-uniform motion is often analyzed using kinematic equations that take into account initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• Examples of non-uniform motion include a car braking to a stop, a ball rolling down a hill, or a plane taking off and landing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uniform Motion**

 
 
• In uniform motion, an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time without changing its speed or direction.
 
• Examples include a car cruising at a constant speed on a straight road or the Earth orbiting the Sun at a constant speed.
 
 
 
• **Circular Motion**
 
 
• This type of motion occurs when an object moves along a circular path at a constant or varying speed.
 
• Examples include the rotation of a fan blade or a satellite orbiting a planet.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Motion**
 
 
• Periodic motion is characterized by the repetition of motion at regular time intervals.
 
• Examples include the swinging of a pendulum or the oscillation of a spring.

questions.question: The laws of motion describe how objects behave when they are in motion. Who among the following is credited with the formulation of these laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isaac Newton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isaac Newton** formulated the **Three Laws of Motion**, which are fundamental principles describing the relationship between the motion of objects and the forces acting on them.
 
• These laws were first introduced in Newton's landmark work, **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica" (The Principia)**, published in **1687**.
 
• The laws of motion laid the groundwork for classical mechanics, which is a branch of physics that deals with the motion of macroscopic objects.
 
• Newton's First Law, also known as the **Law of Inertia**, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• Newton's contributions to physics and mathematics earned him recognition as one of the most influential scientists in history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law:** This law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (**F = ma**). It explains how the motion of an object changes when a force is applied.
 
• **Newton's Third Law:** It states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. This principle is fundamental in understanding interactions between objects.
 
• **Inertia:** A property of matter described in Newton's First Law, where an object resists changes in its state of motion unless influenced by an external force.
 
• **Classical Mechanics:** The branch of physics developed from Newton's laws, which deals with the motion of objects under forces and is used to analyze a wide range of physical phenomena.
 
• **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica:** Often referred to as "The Principia," this book not only introduced the laws of motion but also formulated the law of universal gravitation.

questions.question: If an object is moving along a straight line and with respect to some reference point, its position is x₁ at time t₁ and becomes x₂ at time t₂ . The average velocity of the object during this time interval would be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(x2 - x1 ) / (t2 - t1 )**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The average velocity is defined as the total displacement divided by the total time taken.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as (x2 - x1) / (t2 - t1), where x1 and x2 are the initial and final positions, and t1 and t2 are the initial and final times respectively.
 
• This formula provides a measure of how fast an object is moving along a straight line over a specified time interval.
 
• Average velocity is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• It differs from instantaneous velocity, which refers to the speed of an object at a particular moment in time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement**

 
 
• It is the shortest distance between the initial and final positions of an object.
 
• Displacement is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
• It can be zero even if the distance traveled is non-zero, if the object returns to its starting point.
 
 
 
• **Instantaneous Velocity**
 
 
• It refers to the velocity of an object at a particular instant of time.
 
• Instantaneous velocity can be determined using differential calculus, by taking the derivative of the position function with respect to time.
 
• Unlike average velocity, it provides the speed and direction of an object at a specific moment.
 
 
 
• **Speed vs. Velocity**
 
 
• Speed is a scalar quantity that refers only to how fast an object is moving.
 
• Velocity is a vector quantity that describes both the speed and direction of an object's movement.
 
• Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken, while average velocity is the total displacement divided by the total time taken.
 
 
 
• **Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion**
 
 
• In uniform motion, an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• In non-uniform motion, an object travels unequal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• For non-uniform motion, average velocity can provide an overall description of the motion over a time interval.

questions.question: A cart is moving with a uniform velocity and a retarding force F is applied in the opposite direction to stop the cart. The work done by the force is:

• When a retarding force is applied to a moving object in the opposite direction of its motion, the work done by the force is **negative**.
 
• This is because the force and the displacement of the cart are in opposite directions.
 
• In physics, work done is calculated as the dot product of force and displacement: **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between force and displacement.
 
• For a retarding force, θ = 180°, and cos(180°) = -1, which makes the work done negative.
 
• Negative work indicates that the force is removing energy from the system, slowing the cart down.

• For a retarding force, the kinetic energy of the cart decreases, indicating negative work.

• Friction is a non-conservative force that always does negative work.

• In the absence of non-conservative forces, the total mechanical energy of a system remains constant.
 
• When a retarding force is applied, mechanical energy is converted into other forms like heat.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Friction**
 
 
• Kinetic friction acts opposite to the direction of motion.
 
• It always does negative work, reducing the kinetic energy of the moving object.

• This phenomenon is often referred to as the **law of inertia**, which states that an object will continue in its existing state unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• For example, if a book is lying on a table and balanced forces act on it (gravity and the table's upward force), the book remains stationary.

• Unbalanced forces produce a **net force** that can alter the trajectory of the object.

• Balanced forces do not lead to any change in the **speed or velocity** of an object.

 __

• Examples might include the motion of a ball on a dome-shaped surface, but it is not uniform circular motion.
 
 
 
• **Motion along a straight line**__
 __
 
• This is also known as **linear motion** or **rectilinear motion**.
 
• In this type of motion, an object moves in a straight path without changing its direction.
 
• Examples include a car driving on a straight road or a train moving on straight tracks.
 
 
 
• **Linear motion**__
 
 
• This type of motion refers to the movement of an object in a **straight line**.
 
• Linear motion can be uniform (constant speed) or non-uniform (changing speed).
 
• Examples include the motion of a sprinter running on a straight track or an elevator moving up and down.

questions.question: A body, starting from rest, falls from a building and reaches the ground in 2 secs. What will be the velocity of the body when it reaches the ground? (Acceleration due to gravity = 10 ms⁻² )
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The body starts from rest, so the initial velocity (u) is 0 m/s.
 
• The time (t) taken to reach the ground is 2 seconds.
 
• The acceleration due to gravity (g) is 10 m/s².
 
• The final velocity (v) can be calculated using the formula v = u + gt.
 
• Substituting the values, v = 0 + (10 m/s² * 2 s) = 20 m/s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**

 
 
• It is the acceleration that the Earth imparts to objects due to gravity.
 
• The standard value of g on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s², often rounded to 10 m/s² for simplicity in calculations.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• It is the motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.
 
• In a vacuum, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their masses.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• These equations describe the relationship between displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• Commonly used equations include: v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at², and v² = u² + 2as.
 
 
 
• **Terminal Velocity:**
 
 
• It is the constant speed that a freely falling object eventually reaches when the resistance of the medium prevents further acceleration.
 
• For objects falling through air, terminal velocity depends on the object's size, shape, and mass.
